fundamental.headline: Mixed business, and expensive
fundamental.health: Sales up 15% over the last year, it keeps 23 cents of every sales dollar as free cash, its debt is easily covered by earnings.
fundamental.price_text: You're paying more than usual: its price vs sales is higher than 85% of the last 5 years. Compared with similar companies, adjusted for growth, it's priced about in line.
drivers: It is buying back shares, which grows each shareholder's slice.
news: No major company news in the last two weeks.
fundamental.take: Average business at a premium price: there are better places to put money right now. This is research, not personal advice.

timing.label: No rush

attention.text: Attention: Wikipedia page views 5.5k on 2026-11-06, 0.9× its 30-day normal (6.0k/day) · Hacker News: 0 stories in the last 24h (normal 1.0/day), tone of the last week mixed.

deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 9% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.8% = 10-year Treasury 4.8% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 15% last year; 15%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 39% (3 years ago 19%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $39 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 50% (3 years ago 20%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $1.8B, up 3% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 15%/yr over 3 years and 12%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 31% vs a 5-year range of 17–31% (median 23%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $12.9B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($12.9B buybacks + $0M dividends) = 4.9% of the company's market value. Share count down 3.3% from a year ago (buybacks outpacing stock pay).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $3.77, down 1% in 90 days (down 1% in the last 30); 11 analysts raised, 25 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $3.58, up 0% in 90 days; 18 analysts raised, 12 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers
deeper.text: Compared with 4 peers (META, GOOGL, AMZN, AAPL): sales growth 15% vs a median of 19%; operating margin 31% vs 33%; price/sales 5.2× vs 7.0×.

deeper.title: Insider trading
deeper.text: Last 90 days: no open-market purchases; sales $4.1M, 32% under pre-set 10b5-1 trading plans. Source: SEC Form 4.

deeper.title: New risk factors
deeper.text: 3 new risk-factor headings vs last year's annual report, e.g. “Risk Factors Related to the WBD Transaction”; “The WBD transaction may not be completed on the currently contemplated timeline or terms, or at all.”.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +47% vs a year ago · $3.52 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 47% vs sales 12%: profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 2 quarters running, but the beats are shrinking (1% → 0%): the bar is getting harder to clear.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.read: Sales up 12% from a year ago but slowing (from 16% two quarters ago): the fastest growth may be behind it.
tiles.explain: Growth of quarterly sales (revenue) compared with the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $31 of operating profit, up from $29 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Only 77% of reported profit became spare cash, usually because of heavy investment; worth watching.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 18× last year's profit (lower than 93% of the last 5 years; below peers' 21).
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Jan 19; analysts expect EPS of $0.68, up 21% from a year ago. It usually moves about 6% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.

tiles.title: Company outlook
tiles.read: No numeric outlook was found in the latest earnings release, so the next report carries more surprise risk.
tiles.explain: Guidance = what management says it expects for the next quarter or year, from its 8-K earnings release.

tiles.title: Forecast changes
tiles.read: Next year's EPS forecast is down 1% in 90 days (11 raised, 25 cut lately): forecasts are steady.
tiles.explain: How the average analyst forecast for next year's earnings per share changed (Yahoo, unofficial).
